reference: Bash type/help and the documented ss synopsis define metadata expectations. Socket operations remain deferred to a disposable VM or reviewed sock_diag/proc mock; no iproute2 parity result is claimed.
coverage: Registered as a Bash builtin with the candidate executable search path empty.
Short help exposes the configured ss synopsis.
Extended Bash help exposes the documented subset and process annotation option.
Deferred: numeric TCP/UDP/Unix snapshots and state/family selectors.
Deferred: /proc fallback, process ownership mapping, netlink robustness, and output error handling.
exclusions: No ss operational invocation is made in this environment. Socket queries, --version's sock_diag probe, /proc reads, and error/recovery behavior require the explicitly requested future disposable VM or controlled syscall mock.
No ambient socket table, host /proc path, or real network peer is used.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify ss as a builtin even with the candidate PATH empty, so lookup cannot fall through to an external ss executable.
Bash short help must expose the configured public synopsis for this loadable; the expected line comes from the ss entry in the loadable catalog.
Bash help must include the documented ss subset and -p annotation option from the loadable's long help, not merely register a name.
cases.script: doc=$(help ss); [[ $doc == *"ss(8) subset over NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG."* && $doc == *"-p"* && $doc == *"annotate rows with the holding process"* ]] && printf 'documented-help\n'

cases.purpose: Future operation comparison should cover default TCP selection, TCP/UDP/Unix family flags, listen versus all states, numeric endpoints, and IPv4/IPv6 rows using only sockets owned by the fixture.

Future operation comparison should force sock_diag unavailable and verify deterministic TCP/UDP/Unix proc-table fallback, empty snapshots, queue limitations, and no partial netlink rows after fallback.

Future operation comparison should verify -p associates fixture-owned socket inodes with the correct process and file descriptor, while tolerating denied process directories and descriptors that disappear during scanning.

Future operation comparison should cover multipart sock_diag replies, ACK/EINTR/unmatched sequences, malformed and truncated messages, interrupted dumps, and atomic fallback after an invalid family dump.

Future operation comparison should check buffered output failures, recovery on a later call in the same shell, repeated invocations with different selectors, and --version status when its sock_diag probe or output fails.
